subject.title: [Feature]: First-class org/team deployment — workspace scaffolding, RBAC, and deployment manifests

question: Should OpenClaw core accept first-class org/team deployment as a core security/config product surface, and which pieces should remain in this umbrella versus the narrower open RFCs?
rationale: The request would change Gateway auth, tool-policy, session-state, setup/config, and deployment guarantees; current docs say operator scopes are not hostile multi-tenant isolation, while VISION.md supports security work but warns against heavy orchestration layers.

options.title: Decompose and keep the umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue open as the parent, approve only scoped sub-issues for RBAC, identity, scaffolding, manifests, and docs after deciding the security boundary.

options.title: Route to narrower RFCs
options.body: Close this only after all remaining pieces are represented by viable canonical issues such as per-session policy, tenant isolation, identity modes, and a separate scaffold/manifest item.

options.title: Decline core org deployment
options.body: Document separate Gateways, existing agent bindings, trusted proxy, and plugin/ClawHub paths as the supported model instead of adding first-class core org deployment.

recommendation.title: Decompose and keep the umbrella
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the parent, approve only scoped sub-issues for RBAC, identity, scaffolding, manifests, and docs after deciding the security boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The related conversation identity modes issue and adjacent product/security framing make steipete the best available owner for the direction choice.
